Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We moved fast internally and our security team wants to run the proof-of-concept in an isolated VPC (no internet egress, customer-controlled subnets) to validate data handling. Two asks from security:

- A short extension of the 14-day trial to 30 days so they have time to finish the integration tests.
- A promotional credit pool to cover the Dedicated/Private test run (~$30k of run credits) so we can exercise the private runtime during the window.

They also requested our SOC2 and encryption config be accepted as part of the POC — happy to share any forms. Is this something Redwood can support without reclassifying us into an enterprise contract?

Thanks,

Quick Qs for your security team before we proceed:
- Are you planning on using your own KMS/HSM (bring-your-own-key) or would you use Redwood-managed keys for the POC?
- Expected peak concurrency / tokens per call — helps size the Dedicated pool.

I'll loop in security and sales ops to expedite the approval. Expect a formal note and a temporary billing addendum if approved.

Best,

Evelyn / Dev — I reviewed the questionnaire and the BYOK note. High level:
- BYOK is fine for a time-boxed POC if Velox provides key policy and KMS proofs.
- We require a signed POC security attestation (one-page) that locks the scope: no production data, ephemeral logs retained for 30 days, and egress blocked.
- If they accept our temporary attestation and provide the KMS metadata, we can greenlight the isolated environment.

I'll draft the attestation. Dev — we should validate the Dedicated config (instance types, network ACLs) match their requested egress restrictions before we provision.
